title: smime-tree 0.3.0 pins yanked pkix-chain 0.1.1 — broken for new consumers
description:
smime-tree 0.3.0 was just published with Cargo.toml pinning pkix-chain = { version = "0.1.1" }. That version is YANKED on crates.io (along with 0.1.0). Active pkix-chain versions on crates.io: 0.2.0 (2026-05-06), 0.3.0 (2026-05-08), 0.4.0 (2026-05-08 — current default).

Note: smime-tree 0.2.0 (previously published) has the same yanked-dep flaw — this is a pre-existing bug carried forward, not a regression introduced by this release. But shipping 0.3.0 perpetuates it.

Impact: New consumers who add 'smime-tree = "0.3.0"' to their Cargo.toml will fail dep resolution because Cargo refuses to use yanked versions in fresh resolves. Existing consumers with a Cargo.lock still work.

Repro:
  cargo new test-consumer && cd test-consumer
  cargo add smime-tree
  cargo build  # fails: pkix-chain 0.1.1 yanked

Fix path requires:
1. Pick non-yanked pkix-chain version: 0.4.0 is current/recommended, 0.3.0 also OK, 0.2.0 oldest non-yanked.
2. Audit smime-tree/src/cert.rs and related for any breaking API changes between pkix-chain 0.1.1 and target version. CHANGELOG note from PKIX project says pkix-chain 0.4.0 is 'transitively breaking' due to re-export of pkix-path::ValidatedPath — likely affects map_pkix_error in cert.rs.
3. Update smime-tree/Cargo.toml: pkix-chain = ... new version
4. Run cargo test -p smime-tree, fix any compile/test failures from API drift
5. Bump smime-tree 0.3.0 → 0.3.1 (patch-level dep fix is not breaking for smime-tree's own API)
6. Publish smime-tree 0.3.1
7. Yank smime-tree 0.3.0 (and probably also yank 0.2.0 since it carries the same flaw)

Decision points the user needs to weigh:
- Yank 0.3.0 immediately or leave with a note in README?
- Yank 0.2.0 too?
- Target pkix-chain 0.4.0 (most current) or 0.3.0 (more conservative, smaller API delta)?

Related: this also interacts with MIME-34a (production-readiness gate for pkix-path algorithm coverage). Moving to a current pkix-chain doesn't expand algorithm coverage — the P-384/RSA-PSS gap is still in pkix-path itself. But getting onto a maintained branch positions smime-tree to benefit when pkix-path lands those algorithms.
close_reason: Fixed: smime-tree 0.3.1 published with pkix-chain '0.4' (current). One small code change in cert.rs to use ValidationPolicy::new() constructor because pkix-path 0.3 marked the struct non_exhaustive. Quality gate clean. Yanked 0.3.0, 0.2.0, 0.1.0 (all carry the same yanked-dep flaw). Committed as fefda51 (unpushed).
